title: Provider-terms compliance in model routing
subtitle: A terms-of-service firewall in the agent runtime decides which traffic may reach which provider, so a subscription session is used as its vendor permits.
lede: In Agent Swarm a router picks a model endpoint for every agent request, from my own GPUs or from hosted providers, and some providers' terms forbid automated, unattended back-end use of their models. In an automatic router that rule is easy to break by accident. I made provider terms a routing constraint in code, so compliance does not depend on whoever configures the next endpoint. The rule separates foreground use for a person from automated back-end use, because the terms draw that line.
quote: I put compliance inside the mechanism that could violate it, and I check twice where a mistake would be invisible.
evidence: Model routing with compliance constraints: provider terms enforced in the agent router, separating foreground use for a person from unattended back-end use.
Defence in depth: the terms rule checked at endpoint registration and again on every routing decision, with an explicit no-eligible-endpoint result instead of a guess.
Multi-provider LLM integration: hosted providers presented in the same OpenAI-compatible shape as local GPU models, rate-limited in Redis and self-registering.
author: Corey James
